coverage.note: seen in /research and /learn but not hunted in this test run

findings.title: Server-side JavaScript injection via eval() in POST /contributions
findings.summary: preTax, afterTax and roth from the request body are passed straight to eval(), so any logged-in user (and accounts are open to self-signup) can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js server process.

boundary.attacker: anonymous visitor who self-registers via POST /signup, then any logged-in user
boundary.asset: code execution in the Node.js server process (filesystem, env, DB connection)

locations.note: only isLoggedIn guards the route
open self-registration means the login requirement is no real barrier
only checks that a session userId exists; no role or ownership check
a fresh signup is immediately logged in

locations.quote: const validations = [isNaN(preTax), isNaN(afterTax), isNaN(roth), preTax < 0, afterTax < 0, roth < 0];
locations.note: validation runs only after eval() has already executed the input; not an effective control
urlencoded body (extended: false) delivers the fields as raw strings to eval; no schema validation or CSRF middleware is active (csrf block at server.js:105-114 is commented out)

findings.remediation: Replace eval() with numeric parsing, e.g. parseInt(req.body.preTax, 10), and reject non-integers before use.

findings.title: NoSQL $where injection via threshold query parameter on GET /allocations/:userId
findings.summary: The threshold query parameter is interpolated inside a quoted string in a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression, so any logged-in user (sign-up is open) can rewrite the predicate, e.g. threshold=' || '1'=='1 makes it always true and returns every user's allocation percentages and names in one request, and a looping payload (0';while(true){}') ties up MongoDB JavaScript execution. Server-side JS in MongoDB cannot reach other collections, so the data exposed is the same low-sensitivity allocation data as the IDOR, plus a database availability impact.

boundary.attacker: any logged-in user; accounts are open to self-registration via POST /signup, so effectively unauthenticated
boundary.asset: all users' allocation records with userName/firstName/lastName; MongoDB availability via long-running $where

locations.note: threshold read from query string with no validation
threshold comes from req.query unvalidated
the parseInt/range-check fix exists only inside a comment block (lines 63-76) and is not active
bundled MongoDB 4.4 started without --noscripting, so $where JavaScript is enabled
open self-registration; signup handler sets req.session.userId (session.js:235)

findings.remediation: Do not build $where strings; parse threshold with parseInt, range-check it, and query with {userId: parsedUserId, stocks: {$gt: parsedThreshold}}.

findings.title: IDOR: GET /allocations/:userId returns any user's allocations
findings.summary: The handler takes userId from the URL path instead of the session and performs no ownership check, so any logged-in user can view another user's portfolio allocations and name by changing the path parameter. Severity is medium rather than high because the exposure is read-only and limited to allocation percentages and names; user ids are small sequential integers, so enumeration is trivial.

boundary.attacker: any logged-in user; accounts are open to self-registration via POST /signup, so effectively unauthenticated
boundary.asset: other users' allocation percentages (stocks/funds/bonds) plus userName, firstName, lastName

locations.note: userId taken from URL, not req.session
only checks that a session userId exists; no role or ownership check
open self-registration; signup handler sets req.session.userId (session.js:235)

locations.quote: // Fix for A4 Insecure DOR -  take user id from session instead of from URL param
locations.note: the session-based fix is commented out
user ids are sequential integers, so other users' ids are guessable

findings.remediation: Use req.session.userId (or compare req.params.userId to it and return 403 on mismatch).

findings.title: Missing admin authorization on GET/POST /benefits
findings.summary: The benefits routes are guarded only by isLoggedIn although an isAdmin middleware exists, so any user can list all non-admin users and change any user's benefitStartDate by supplying an arbitrary userId in the POST body.

boundary.attacker: any logged-in non-admin user; accounts are open to self-registration via POST /signup, so effectively unauthenticated
boundary.asset: all non-admin users' benefitStartDate (write) and their ids, first and last names (read)

locations.note: admin guard exists but is not applied to these routes
userId comes from req.body
only checks that a session userId exists; no role or ownership check
a working admin check (user.isAdmin from DB) exists but is not wired to /benefits
target userId and new date are taken from the request body with no ownership or role check
open self-registration; signup handler sets req.session.userId (session.js:235)

findings.remediation: Add isAdmin to both routes: app.get("/benefits", isLoggedIn, isAdmin, ...) and app.post("/benefits", isLoggedIn, isAdmin, ...) (the fix is already present as a comment at app/routes/index.js:57-60).
